headline.purpose: Whose turn it is; grows on your own turn.

title.purpose: Lobby section heads, the top standing's name, the small wordmark on the band.

label.purpose: Buttons, pad row names, seat names.

action.purpose: The big primary action in the tray.

score.purpose: Numbers written on the pad in the player's ink, tabular figures.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default for state changes and things arriving.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Loops: waiting dots, the chosen chip breathing.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Gentle overshoot for things that pop into place (roll dots).

motion.name: ease-develop
motion.purpose: A new score coming into focus (1300ms).

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Theme change, meter fill, roll dots.

motion.name: spring-snappy
motion.purpose: Panels, tabs, toggles, the segmented pill.

motion.name: sparkle
motion.purpose: Yatzy and winner bursts; decoration only.

motion.name: reduced-motion

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Score Pad Rows
components.description: Rows on the ruled pad: a score you could take (lilac chip), a zero (dashed chip), the box you picked (violet), and a written score in the player's ink.

narrative.overview:
A family game night after dark, set on a clean, modern table: dark plum around the edges, lavender for whatever is yours or chosen, and one soft pink for the thing to do next. The evening theme is the main scene, because the game is mostly played on evening voice calls. The daytime theme keeps the same structure with pale lavender ground and plum ink, so both themes share one set of roles and differ only in values.

The screens are calm and roomy: soft raised white or plum sheets, pill-shaped controls, a plum band or plate holding the wordmark, and a 3D tray of porcelain dice with violet pips on violet felt. Femininity comes from the palette and the rounded display face, kept light: no ornament, no texture on the interface, no illustration. The playful moments are short and earned, like the sparkle burst on a Yatzy and on the winner's name, the pulse of your tint when your turn arrives, and a new score coming into focus on the pad.

Rejected looks the owner confirmed on rendered screens: the earlier candy-shop identity (candy names, colors, motifs) and the "Sunprint" cyanotype that followed it (script typefaces, paper or print textures, anything old-fashioned). A personal aquarium, shown as a realistic glass tank beside the dice, is planned and has no visual system yet.
keyCharacteristics: Plum, lavender and one pink, in a daytime and an evening theme generated from one palette file.
Quicksand 700 for names and big moments; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything you read and tap.
Soft raised sheets with plum-tinted shadows; pills for every button.
Each player owns a flower or leaf tint that rings their face, colors their cup and writes their numbers.
Short, earned celebrations; reduced motion turns all of them into fades.

rules.name: The One Pink Rule
rules.body: Pink marks the single thing to do next, plus the earned +35 bonus. If two pink buttons are on screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Lavender Is Yours Rule
rules.body: Violet and lavender mean chosen, selected, focused or earned. They never decorate.

rules.name: The One Palette File Rule
rules.body: Every color comes from `theme/palette.ts` as a generated CSS variable, and every text pairing there passes 4.5:1 in a test. A new color is added there with its pairing, never typed into a component.

rules.name: The Ink, Not Hue Rule
rules.body: A player's hue never sets text on the pad; only its per-theme ink does.

rules.name: The Rounded Moments Rule
rules.body: Quicksand is for names and moments: wordmark, section heads, the turn headline, the winner, the Yatzy word. Controls, tables and numbers stay in Atkinson.

rules.name: The 17px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text is smaller than 1.0625rem, and every size is in rem so the Text size setting scales the whole UI.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow mixes `--shadow` at low opacity with negative spread. No pure black, no hard offset shadows.

rules.name: The Press-Down Rule
rules.body: The primary action sits on a darker lip (accent mixed 22% toward black) and presses down 0.12rem when pressed or while the dice roll; it jiggles while you hold to shake.

dos: Do take every color from `theme/palette.ts` and add any new text pairing to its contrast test (4.5:1).
Do keep pink to the single next action and the earned bonus; use violet/lavender for chosen, selected, focused and earned.
Do write player numbers in their tint's ink for the current theme, and use the hue only for rings, swatches, dots, tab washes and the cup.
Do set names, headlines and big moments in Quicksand 700, and everything you read or tap in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next.
Do make every button a pill at least 48px tall, and every surface a soft sheet with the plum-tinted shadow.
Do keep sizes in rem with nothing under 1.0625rem.
Do design both themes at once, evening first, and judge a new look on rendered screens.
Do keep celebrations short and decorative, and make reduced motion turn them into fades.
donts: Don't use script typefaces, paper or print textures, or anything old-fashioned.
Don't bring back candy names, candy colors or candy motifs; femininity stays a light touch.
Don't type a hex value into a component or stylesheet.
Don't use a player's hue as text on the pad.
Don't use pure-black or hard offset shadows.
Don't make it look like a casino or a slot machine; it is a calm evening game among family.
